title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout facts, billing qualifications and documented controls are supported. Both API calls match Microsoft's documentation, and independent searches found no documented node-specific tenant switch or automation for the human-assistance setting.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost

claims.quote: The harness used to build this agent uses usage-based billing. Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Credit usage is charged to the environment where the work runs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Allocating credits and clearing tenant-pool draw contains an environment's prepaid consumption.
claims.quote: To contain prepaid consumption, allocate a defined amount of Copilot Credits to the environment and turn off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: Turning off tenant-pool draw does not prevent usage through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't prevent consumption through a pay-as-you-go billing plan linked to the environment.

claims.claim: Azure budgets alert without stopping Copilot Studio usage.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: Environment allocation controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, including other agents, workflows and prompts.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness. Configure controls with the other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in mind for each environment.

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or equivalent licensing-and-capacity permissions.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The node page names no licence among its prerequisites for adding the node.
claims.quote: Searched: read the complete /microsoft-copilot-studio/workflows-experience/agent-node-workflow page, including its opening billing note and Add an agent node steps. No prerequisite licence is named; billing is addressed by the linked billing pages.

claims.claim: The tenant-draw control is at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: select Licensing. ... Under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Copilot Credits. ... Select the environment. ... Under Capacity overages, clear Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes the environment allocation.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01" ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The allocation request identifies the environment through scope.environmentId.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId }

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: allocation request body
claims.claim: The Copilot Credits entitlement in allocatedEntitlements is MCSMessages.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID MCSMessages and are managed through the licensing/allocationsV2 operations of the Power Platform API.

claims.claim: The request sets allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity, with 5000 used as an example.
claims.quote: allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages" allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 }

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: allocation request body
claims.claim: Setting enforcementRules[].ruleType to TenantPool with enabled false turns off tenant-pool draw.
claims.quote: enforcementRules = @( ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ... )

claims.claim: The allocation operation requires authenticated authorisation.
claims.quote: $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" }

claims.claim: The allocation example sends Content-Type application/json.
claims.quote: -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.claim: A published environment group rule makes the environment's tenant-draw setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center

claims.claim: Programmatic requests cannot override the group-governed tenant-draw setting.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Tenant-pool draw is selected by default for eligible Copilot Studio environments without allocation configuration.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, Draw from the available capacity in my tenant is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.claim: No central enforcement setting for Request human assistance when unsure is documented as of November 2026.
